item.title: 'You have no right to comment on my private life' - Kevin De Bruyne hits back at Napoli exit rumours amid PSV Eindhoven transfer links
item.description: SSC Napoli v Torino FC - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Kevin De Bruyne has hit out at the Italian media for creating a hostile environment for his family amid ongoing speculation regarding his future at Napoli. The Belgian playmaker spoke out ahead of a highly anticipated return to the Etihad Stadium for a Champions League encounter with his former club, Manchester City. Frustration over privacy and transfer links De Bruyne has expressed his deep frustration with recent reports suggesting he could leave the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in the January transfer window . The veteran playmaker, who has been linked with a move to PSV Eindhoven, used his pre-match press conference to address a recent interview given by his wife in Belgium that he feels was intentionally misinterpreted by the Italian press to fuel exit rumours. "I’m quite sorry about it all to be honest. If you go and read the article, which you have not read, you will understand what she said. I was away in Belgium and then a lot of things were being said and there were a lot of negative reactions towards my wife," De Bruyne said, as quoted by Football Italia . He voiced specific anger over the publication of photos of his private residence, adding, "I saw photos of my house in the press, which is not good. I know that journalists in Italy have created this situation and I don’t know why. You do not know my private life, you have no right to comment on my private life. It was an unpleasant situation for me and my wife." The veteran playmaker tight-lipped on Napoli future De Bruyne has remained tight-lipped over his long-term future with Napoli, admitting that his approaching 36th birthday leaves him with plenty to weigh up amid his ongoing contract situation . Despite the uncertainty surrounding his next move, the veteran midfielder insisted his focus remains firmly on giving everything for the Partenopei. Rather than getting drawn into speculation, the Belgian playmaker stressed that his immediate priority is maintaining his strong form and helping the club navigate a demanding campaign. "I can’t say very much at this point. I’ve played at 400% so far. I’m not 20 years old anymore, I’m almost 36, so there are lots of things to consider. Right now, there’s not a lot to say. I’m playing well, I’m trying to help the team to do well. There have been lots of challenges this year and a lot of things have happened," he explained. Tactical evolution and return to Manchester Despite the off-field distractions, De Bruyne insisted he is satisfied with his individual performances for Massimiliano Allegri's side this season. item.description: Dortmund and Chelsea target Williams-Barnett set for Tottenham contract extension Borussia Dortmund appear to have lost out in the race for Luca Williams-Barnett, according to a report in the Telegraph. The 18-year-old is believed to be on the verge of agreeing a long-term contract extension with his current employers Tottenham Hotspur. Fellow Premier League outfit Chelsea alongside the Westphalians are believed to have recently made inquiries for the midfielder. Other high-profile clubs such as Bayern Munich, Manchester City and Manchester United have also been linked with him. The England U-19 international has made his first three Premier League appearances for Spurs in recent weeks, scoring once.

item.description: Stats: Here’s how Barcelona have fared without Lamine Yamal in the squad Hansi Flick will face his first Barcelona match without Lamine Yamal this season when the Catalans travel to Azerbaijan to meet Sabah in the Champions League on Wednesday, November 25. The 19-year-old winger has been ruled out because of mild discomfort in his right ankle, with the club confirming that his absence is a precautionary measure and that he is expected to return against Deportivo on Sunday. Yamal’s absence ends an uninterrupted run of 17 appearances in Barcelona’s official matches this season, having accumulated 1,445 minutes, scoring 13 goals and providing 13 assists. However, the German manager has previous experience managing without his most influential young forward, and Barcelona’s results suggest the squad has gradually become better equipped to cope with his absence. Barcelona’s record without Lamine Yamal under Hansi Flick Since Flick took charge, Barcelona have played 17 matches without Yamal, recording 11 victories, five defeats and one draw. During the 2024/25 campaign, Barcelona struggled to maintain consistency without their right winger. They won just two of five matches, beating Brest 3-0 in the Champions League and Barbastro 4-0 in the Copa del Rey. The remaining three fixtures exposed their difficulties, as defeats against Real Sociedad and Atletico Madrid, alongside a draw against Celta Vigo, left Flick with limited reasons for optimism when his teenage forward was unavailable. Barcelona improved considerably during the 2025/26 season The picture changed significantly in 2025/26 when Barcelona collected nine victories from the 12 matches Yamal missed. Notably, their ability to produce positive results without him was particularly evident before his season-ending injury in April. Flick’s side defeated Newcastle United, Valencia, Getafe, Real Oviedo and Slavia Prague during earlier spells without the winger. Sevilla provided a notable exception, handing Barcelona a 1-4 defeat. Yamal’s subsequent hamstring injury forced him to miss the final six league fixtures. Barcelona won four of those matches, overcoming Getafe 2-0, Osasuna 2-1, Real Madrid 2-0 and Real Betis 3-1. item.title: Real Madrid president was ‘obsessed’ with French winger in the summer; will return on one condition – Romano
item.description: Real Madrid president was ‘obsessed’ with French winger in the summer; will return on one condition – Romano Real Madrid’s pursuit of Michael Olise last summer was no secret, and every move the club made towards the player was public knowledge throughout the saga. Eventually, however, the deal did not move ahead as Bayern Munich refused to sell Olise despite the player deeply longing for a move to Real Madrid. Eventually, Los Blancos brought in Yan Diomande for a record transfer fee and the player has settled into Jose Mourinho’s dynamics well. Yet, there have been talks of Olise still being a potential target Florentino Perez is attached to. The latest information As reported by the ever-reliable Fabrizio Romano (h/t Madrid Xtra ) now, Olise was a massive obsession for Perez last summer, and that was the foundation for all of Real Madrid’s persistent efforts. Perez was obsessed with Olise. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) To date, everyone at Real Madrid is said to be ‘in love’ with Olise and what he brings to the field, especially Perez. As for the player’s future, Bayern Munich are set to offer Olise a new contract renewal soon and it remains to be seen what the player decides. At this point, his decision will steer Real Madrid’s interest. Los Blancos continue to be deeply interested in signing him, but will only take a step forward and negotiate with Olise if Bayern Munich inform them that he is for sale. They will preserve relations with the German club as their priority. An atrocious price tag Olise will be offered a renewal. (Photo by Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images) As relayed earlier this month, the Bavarians have now set their asking fee for a potential Olise departure, and the sum will send the eyes of most clubs across the world rolling. The German champions, after all, are said to have placed a €300 million price tag on the Frenchman, and see that to be fair compensation for his services. Needless to say, however, that sum is simply unheard of and not feasible even for Real Madrid. Real Madrid, in that sense, were said to have taken a step back in the race after hearing the price. If Olise can push Bayern and have them admit he is for sale, however, the power dynamics of the saga will shift significantly and give Real Madrid more skin in the game.

item.title: Agit Kabayel is the ringmaster of a new heavyweight circus
item.description: There was a time when an American was in one corner of every single heavyweight world-title fight. Every fight from the end of the bare-knuckle period to the end of the 1980s. The fall of the Wall and the arrival of the Eastern Bloc boxers changed the landscape forever, but still Americans held the grip on a title that seemed forever destined to be owned by a man from Philadelphia or Houston or Louisville. That is all over now, possibly gone for good. Deontay Wilder was the last American heavyweight world champion, and he was beaten in seven rounds by Tyson Fury in early 2020; he challenged Fury the following year, lost again, and that was the last time an American came anywhere near the world heavyweight title. Agit Kabayel after stopping Zhilei Zhang in early 2025 (Getty) Close to 30 years ago, Don King announced that he was searching for the next American heavyweight superstar; that desperate search is continuing today, and at the same time gyms in Tirana, Moscow and Lagos are full of heavyweight dreamers. This Saturday, in front of 50,000 fans in Dusseldorf , Germany’s Agit Kabayel defends his WBC heavyweight title when he meets the unbeaten Nelson Hysa of Albania. It is a bizarrely cosmopolitan clash. Kabayel, on his way directly to the WBC title, stopped in succession a Russian, a Chinese fighter, a Croatian, a Pole, and a Cuban. There is not an American heavyweight left to come even close to pushing Kabayel. The top American is arguably a man called Michael Hunter, who is 38 and had his best win in 2018. Hunter is the only American worth a top-20 ranking, and he is lost in a turbulent sea of boxers from a dozen countries. A Nigerian, an Australian and about seven British boxers are in front of Hunter. Where is Rocky Balboa when you need him? Right now, Kabayel might just be the best of the four heavyweight champions, with Daniel Dubois , Filip Hrgovic and Murat Gassiev holding the other belts in the wake of Oleksandr Usyk giving up all of the gold . And Kabayel, 34, can look good against Hysa who, at 42, is wandering close to George Foreman’s ancient territory. It will be fun until Kabayel does his thing and breaks Hysa’s heart after about six rounds of body shots. Kabayel started three of his last four bouts as the underdog, fighting men with unbeaten records or a genuine claim to a higher ranking. On each occasion, he slowly prodded away and calmly broke the spirit and desire of a trio of quality men. A similar win against Hysa, who is a big lump and offers a lot of bulk for Kabayel to target, will raise Kabayel’s profile against the other champions. item.title: The Davis Cup is broken but Carlos Alcaraz can save it
item.description: For nearly five months of this year, Carlos Alcaraz was sidelined, nursing a wrist injury which threatened to derail his entire season. Just three months on from his return, and despite managing two different injury concerns, the Spaniard has rewritten the history books and could yet send another record tumbling before signing off for Christmas. Four days after claiming his first ATP Finals title, becoming the youngest man – at just 23 – to complete the clean sweep of all four majors and the season-ending individual crown, he could join only Andre Agassi , Novak Djokovic , and Roger Federer in the pantheon of greats to also win the Davis Cup . The tennis calendar doesn’t so much slow to a halt over Christmas as barrel almost cleanly through into the next season, with a rapid turnaround for those heading from the ATP Finals in Turin to the Davis Cup in Bologna this week. But despite Alcaraz’s frenetic autumn schedule, winning three back-to-back tournaments in Vienna, Paris, and Turin, and the wear and tear on his body, he is in spellbinding form and highly fancied to lead Spain to a first title since 2019. The Davis Cup has struggled for relevance in recent years. The fact that it takes place annually lowers the stakes and drama of what claims to be the ‘World Cup’ of tennis, while the torturously convoluted system of play-offs and qualifying ties makes it difficult for the casual fan to understand. Add to that top players’ reluctance to risk injury, and their prioritising of the ATP Tour in an utterly relentless calendar, means the big names tend to drop out and viewers’ interest follows the same downward curve. So it is a huge boost to the tournament that although home star Jannik Sinner remains a long-term absentee, Alcaraz, who missed last year’s Finals, is back, while the Italians – led again by Flavio Cobolli – are fielding a raft of top names including Matteo Berrettini and Lorenzo Musetti . In total, nine top-10 players across both singles and doubles will take part, and seven of the singles top-20. Three-time defending champions Italy face underdogs South Korea before taking on either Felix Auger-Aliassime ’s Canada or Czechia, spearheaded by the top-20 pairing of Jakub Mensik and Jiri Lehecka. The bottom half sees Germany and Spain take on Great Britain and Austria respectively. GB are playing their last tie under the leadership of Leon Smith , who will end a near-17 year stint as captain after this week . There are no faces left from the Finals-winning squad of 2015, the zenith of Smith’s tenure, but there is an exciting mix of the old and new: this year’s breakout British star, Wimbledon semi-finalist Arthur Fery , alongside stalwart Cameron Norrie . Most significantly, GB possess a lethal doubles partnership in world No 1 Henry Patten and No 3 Neal Skupski , who between them have won three of the last four Grand Slams. item.title: 49ers win in Mexico and Bills stay top - NFL week 11
item.description: The San Francisco 49ers and Buffalo Bills remain the pacesetters in each conference of the NFL after both won again. The 49ers beat the Minnesota Vikings in the last of a record nine international games this season to take their record to 9-1. They lead the way in the NFC, with the Chicago Bears and their divisional rivals the Detroit Lions next best on 8-2. Buffalo improved to 9-1 for the first time since 1991 and lead the AFC from another pair of divisional rivals, with the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos on 8-2. The Cincinnati Bengals are 7-3 after being undone by a walk-off field goal for the Washington Commanders. 49ers outsmart Vikings defence Mexico hosted the first regular-season game to be played outside the US in October 2005, and the NFL returned to the country on Sunday following a four-year absence. After being redeveloped for the 2026 World Cup, the Azteca Stadium staged its sixth NFL game and the third involving San Francisco, who kicked off this season's international series by beating the Los Angeles Rams in Australia in week one. Sunday's game pitted the league's best offence against the best defence and was the first international game to be played in the primetime slot. The Vikings defence had not conceded more than 23 points in a game this season, but the 49ers offence outsmarted them in front of 85,612 fans in Mexico City. The 49ers scored four touchdowns in the first half - two by George Kittle - before running out 35-10 winners. Mike Evans returned after missing three games with an Achilles problem to finish with 109 receiving yards and a touchdown. With the game played at high altitude - about 7,220ft (2,240m) above sea level - some players used oxygen masks on the sidelines. San Francisco face another test of their Super Bowl credentials next Sunday at home to the defending champions, the 6-4 Seattle Seahawks, who were one of six teams on their bye this week. San Francisco linebacker Fred Warner has Mexican heritage and his first name is Federico [Getty Images] Giants secure statement win The Jacksonville Jaguars entered week 11 with the best regular-season record over the past 12 months - they had lost only twice - and had scored more than 30 points in each of their past four games. Yet the New York Giants managed to stifle the Jaguars for three quarters and led 20-6 heading into what proved to be a dramatic final quarter. The Jaguars had to settle for a field goal after a controversial call denied them a touchdown, but they still threatened a fightback as they cut the deficit to five. The Giants offence did enough to stop the Jags getting one more possession, though, and secure a 23-18 home win. It was the first time the NFC East leaders have beaten a team with a winning record this season and they are now 6-3-1, while the 7-3 Jags remain in charge of the AFC South. item.title: JJ Redick Credits Lakers’ Early-Season Success To One Special Factor
item.description: Nov 23, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick in the second half against the Utah Jazz at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images The Utah Jazz are among the few teams the Los Angeles Lakers have lost to this season. Although they lost to Utah on Wednesday , the Purple and Gold redeemed themselves on Monday night, posting a 109-94 victory to improve to 15-3 for the season. Monday night’s win was a product of several factors, one of which was Luka Doncic ‘s sustained offensive brilliance . With 28 points, four rebounds, eight assists, and a steal, the Lakers’ superstar led the winning effort. Even so, one could argue that this win belonged to the role players. The grit and hustle shown by players like Jake LaRavia , Matisse Thybulle , Ziaire Williams , and Collin Sexton at key moments defined the Lakers’ performance. During his postgame press conference , head coach JJ Redick had to acknowledge this. While speaking about what makes this team special, Redick stated: “I think they’re all really grateful to be here, the Lakers. They’re all really grateful to be on this team and be a part of the group. I know Matisse has expressed that to me on a couple of occasions.” “You know, for Z, Matisse, and Q, they’ve experienced adversity in their careers in different ways. I think that gratitude piece is like, they’re all in a situation- Jake, we’ve been around him enough to know. But they’re all in a situation where they put the team first, and they’re putting their egos aside.” “That stuff matters,” Redick continued. “It’s one of the reasons our group has had early success because we said on day one, we wanted this season to be about the team and not any one individual, and so far, it’s been that.” As Redick mentioned, much of the Lakers’ approach this year has been guided by the shared common goal. From the roster-building approach to the team-building activities led by Luka Doncic in the summer, the Purple and Gold have prioritized the whole rather than the individual. To that end, the results early in the campaign have been promising. While L.A. is clearly Doncic’s team, with the superstar logging unreal performances on a nightly basis, the contributions of the role players have been beyond critical. Whether this involves Sexton’s hustle, Thybulle’s disruptive work , Grimes’ scoring outbursts , or Williams’ two-way contributions, the Lakers have benefited greatly from the unit’s willingness to make sacrifices for the team. item.description: LAHAINIA, HI- NOVEMBER 23: JJ Mandaquit #23 of the Arizona Wildcats drives to the basket against Justin Menard #3 of the Colorado State Rams in the second half during a first round Southwest Maui Invitational college basketball game at the Lahaina Civic Center on November 23, 2026 in Lahaina, Hawaii. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images With three games in three days, Tommy Lloyd had a goal of giving his bench more playing time to ease the burden off his starting five. Lloyd did play the reserves more than in the previous two outings, but a pesky Colorado State team kept him from subbing as much as he’d have liked. No. 8 Arizona beat the Rams 96-83 on Monday night in its opening game of the Maui Invitational. The Wildcats (5-1) will face Providence, which beat VCU in overtime earlier in the tourney, at 3 p.m. MT Tuesday in the semifinals. All five starters scored in double figures for the UA, with Ivan Kharchenkov having another all-around masterful performance with 24 points, six rebounds, six assists and four steals. Caleb Holt went for 20 with nine rebounds and four assists, while Motiejus Krivas had 17 with seven rebounds and five assists, JJ Mandaquit scored a career-high 15 and Derek Dixon chipped in 10. Mandaquit, a Hawai’i native playing in front of roughly 50 friends and family, was 5 of 7 from the field and 4 of 6 from 3. He’s 11 of 22 from outside this season. Arizona shot 54.7 percent overall and made 12 of 27 3s, getting multiple triples from four players for the first time since the 2024 NCAA Tournament opener against Akron. item.description: The Cincinnati Bengals are a solid team. They're capable of being great. But they simply refuse to commit to what it takes to achieve greatness. Run. The. Damn. Ball. No thanks, says Zac Taylor and Joe Burrow . Be it the head coach's stubbornness or the quarterback's arrogance – or vice versa – the Bengals just won't commit to running the ball even when the game situation calls for it. And their refusal to run the ball and control the clock late in the game cost the Bengals in a 22-20 loss to the Washington Commanders on Oct. 23 at rain-soaked Northwest Stadium in suburban D.C. It was Cincinnati's first loss since Oct. 4 vs. Jacksonville. Remember what happened that day? The Bengals refused to run the ball. Mark the Washington game down as another example of why the Bengals probably aren't going to win the Super Bowl this season. If ever there was a game to run the ball more, it was on a wet and windy night against a gritty but inferior opponent. But Taylor and Burrow couldn't be bothered to run a balanced offense. It's like they can't help themselves. They insist on showing the world on almost every play that the Bengals are a great passing team, even though everyone already knows that. The Bengals ran the ball one time in the fourth quarter, failing to protect a one-point lead and milk the clock. Cincinnati held a 17-16 lead when it took possession of the ball with 10:27 remaining. Burrow proceeded to throw the ball five times for 23 yards. No running plays. The Bengals only ate up 2 minutes and 2 seconds before having to punt. A run play or two could've taken, say, an extra 46 seconds off the clock. item.title: Predators’ Struggle to Recapture Early Season Power-Play Success
item.description: Jonathan Marchesault and Filip Forsberg celebrate goal against Ottowa October 2026 Getty The Nashville Predators were a top-three team in power-play percentage throughout October, but have since hit a cold spell this month. The Preds had a 33.3% power-play percentage at their peak in October, ranking them third-best in the NHL. Since then, they have steadily fallen, going just 4-for-30 over their last 30 power-play opportunities and dropping to ninth in the NHL (24.7%). The Predators’ Power Play Nashville’s primary power play unit consists of Steven Stamkos, Ryan O’Reilly, Jonathan Marchessault, Roman Josi and Filip Forsberg. On paper, the five make perfect sense, comprising four of the team’s top five players in points , with the outlier being Marchessault, who missed two weeks with an injury and still ranks seventh. The rotation worked perfectly in October as well, helping keep them near the top of the Central Division, where they currently reside. The goal-scoring ability of Steven Stamkos, who sits fifth all-time in power-play goals scored , paired with the veteran playmaking of Forsberg, O’Reilly, and Josi, was extremely efficient, but that production hasn’t been there of late. Stamkos has been the only power-play goal scorer on the team in November, as the Predators have gone 3-25 on opportunities (12%), putting them in the bottom five for the month . Still sitting at 12-6-5 on the year, the Predators have managed to succeed despite their recently slumping power play, winning six straight to start the month of November. However, power plays are an important part of a team’s success, as consistently scoring with the man advantage is almost required for any playoff-contending team. What Needs to Change With the amount of top-heavy veteran experience on the Predators’ roster, it seems they might just have to ride out the slump and hope the power play finds its way back. Currently still the ninth-best in the NHL, Nashville knows its power play was once one of its strongest aspects. However, since then, the defense has stepped up while the power play has gone ghost. Filled with veterans providing a large majority of the team’s points, Nashville has to keep its faith in them and hope they can begin to click again. Breaking the slump starts with getting Marchessault more involved and continuing to feed the historically prolific power-play scorer, Steven Stamkos. The return of Jonathan Marchessault has been a recent boost to the offense with a goal in each of his last two games , and Nashville will need him to bring that same impact to its 5-on-4 play to get back to full power. Currently sitting tied for third in the Central Division in points, Nashville could put itself in a key position to snap its two-year playoff drought if it can return to a top-five power play while retaining its recent defensive and goaltending strengths. Pep Guardiola was Manchester City’s figurehead and manager for the past decade. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office.
